title: WildfireGuardian benchmark descriptor
description: Metadata for a single benchmark case. One benchmark.yaml lives in every benchmark directory alongside README.md, inputs/ and expected/.

benchmark_id.description: Stable identifier. Never reused, never renumbered.

label.description: Family label from the design document, e.g. F5 or K11.

solver.description: Identifier of the reference solver that turns inputs/ into a result document.

inputs.description: Named input documents, given as paths relative to the benchmark directory.

assumptions.description: Semantic switches the expected answer depends on. A benchmark whose answer changes under a different convention MUST state the convention here.

expected_behavior.description: Headline expected values, duplicated from expected/expected.yaml for readability. Consistency is enforced by tests.

tolerance.description: Numeric tolerances. 'default' applies everywhere; other keys override by leaf name or dotted result path. A scalar is an absolute tolerance; {abs: .., rel: ..} sets both.

exactness.description: How the expected answer was obtained, and therefore how much it is worth. CLOSED_FORM: an analytic expression derived by hand (elementary functions, erf and log included), exact to machine precision. FINITE_ENUMERATION: exhaustive enumeration of a finite set; no approximation. NUMERIC_REFERENCE: a numerical procedure with a declared, analytically justified error bound - never a Monte Carlo estimate. SEEDED_STOCHASTIC_VALIDATION: reproducible given the seed and checked within a stated Monte Carlo band. A Monte Carlo approximation is never described as exact.

detects.description: Failure-mode identifiers this benchmark is designed to catch.

mutations_expected_to_fail.description: Mutation ids from wg_benchmarks.mutations that this benchmark must detect.

hand_checkable.description: True when a competent reviewer can verify the expected answer with pen and paper in a few minutes.

information_structure.description: Declared structure of a benchmark that involves uncertainty. Optional, and absent from every deterministic benchmark. Where present it names the pieces of the probabilistic problem so that a reader can see which of point prediction, distribution, ensemble, posterior and decision the benchmark is actually about.
